newsitem.title: UK: Lover of 1960s UK fashion guru jailed for killing.
newsitem.headline: Lover of 1960s UK fashion guru jailed for killing.

text.p: The lover of flamboyant 1960s fashion designer Ossie Clark was found guilty on Monday of killing him in a frenzied knife attack last year at the shabby London flat they once shared.
Diego Cogolato, 29, had admitted manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility. He was jailed for six years.

He had stabbed 54-year-old Clark more than 40 times and beaten him about the head on August 6 last year. Cogolato's lawyers said he had been in a psychotic state induced by a combination of illegal and legal drugs.
Italian-born Cogolato had told police after his arrest that he had heard voices from God telling him to kill his former lover. He and Clark had separated some months earlier, but had remained close.

Clark fell from being one of the brightest stars of swinging 1960s London to impoverished obscurity. Elizabeth Taylor and Mick and Bianca Jagger were among the celebrities who wore his swirling, diaphanous designs at the height of his fame.
But his artistic talents were not matched by business acumen and ambitious ventures, such as plans for a chain of his own shops in Beverly Hills, Munich, Zurich and New York, foundered.
Clark separated from his wife and collaborator, fabric designer Celia Birtwhistle, in 1974 after a five-year marriage. They had two sons.
Early in their marriage, the couple had posed for one David Hockney's most famous paintings, in which Clark was shown long-haired and barefoot with his cat on his lap.
In later years, the Liverpool-born designer only made the headlines when his often eccentric behaviour got him into trouble with the police.
